I am reviewing the Monopoly game state to prepare a decision.

I have $523 and am on INDIANA_AVENUE. I own the pink and orange property sets, but NEW_YORK_AVENUE is mortgaged. I need to unmortgage it before building. Other players are cash-poor.

p2 owns Boardwalk and railroads but lacks Park Place. p3 has hotels on Med/Baltic and Pacific, plus a brown monopoly. p4 has light blue hotels and nearly a yellow set.

I am mapping the color sets to check for monopolies. p4 owns Virginia, so the pink set is split. p2 has NC and Marvin Gardens in yellow. p4 also holds Kentucky, while p2 owns Indiana (mortgaged) and Illinois is unowned.

I am checking the remaining color sets. Atlantic is unowned, so the yellow set is incomplete. The green set is split between p3 and p2. I have Water Works and p3 has Electric Company. I also need to verify my cash balance after recent rent.

I cannot build yet because the orange set is incomplete. I will unmortgage NEW_YORK_AVENUE for $110 and cash will drop to $413. Building costs $100 per house per property.

Building one house on each orange property costs $300, leaving $113. I am weighing whether to build or wait until I can reach three houses. p4's light blue hotels are worth $550–$600, which could bankrupt me with only $113 left. I need to decide if the extra rent is worth that risk.

I calculated the exact numbers. Unmortgaging New York and building three houses would leave me with $113 cash plus $215 in mortgageable assets, totaling $328 liquidity. That is still below the $550 hotel rent from p4. I would go bankrupt if I build now. I will keep my current cash and wait for a safer moment.

I will mortgage my pink properties and Water Works only if I land on a light blue hotel. With $523 cash, I can cover the Baltic hotel but not Connecticut or Oriental/Vermont. Adding the $215 in mortgageable assets brings total liquidity to $738, which covers one light blue hotel with a small buffer.

I am evaluating trade options. p4 would not sell Virginia cheaply, and the pink set is weaker than orange. p2 owns Boardwalk but would likely want Park Place back to complete dark blue, so I will not sell it. p3 holds Pacific and Electric Company, which could be useful.

I ruled out trading with p3 because they would not give me anything useful. I also rejected a deal with p2 since they want Park Place back and I have no properties they need. I am now considering selling something to raise cash for building the orange set.

I need $1010 to build three houses on orange. Mortgageable assets would only cover $738, leaving a $272 shortfall and zero cash afterward. Selling Park Place is too risky because it would complete p2's dark blue set or strengthen p4. I am now considering trading my pink properties for cash plus Virginia from p4.

I rejected trading my pink properties for cash. Completing the pink set would let p4 build hotels immediately and create another dangerous threat. No one can easily complete the green set either. I will end my turn and wait.

I am reconsidering the trade strategy. p2 has only $264 and just paid $550 rent, so they are vulnerable to bankruptcy. If p2 lands on a hotel this turn, I would inherit Boardwalk and complete dark blue. p3 is safe with $813 and brown hotels.

I realized that unmortgaging New York Avenue would not immediately improve my rent. If any orange property is mortgaged, the entire orange monopoly cannot collect double rent. I will end my turn without unmortgaging.

I will not mortgage my pink properties or Water Works preemptively. The expected rent gain is too small to justify the cost, and I would still lack enough cash to survive a light blue hotel hit.

I am now considering an alliance with p2 and p3 against p4. p3's brown hotels are less dangerous because players land there infrequently near GO.

I considered selling Water Works to p3 for cash. A utility monopoly would only raise rent by $40–$120, and even $200 would leave me with $723 total. That is still below the $900 needed to build three houses on orange, so this trade does not solve my liquidity problem.

The total cash needed to safely build three houses on orange is $1610. I have only $738 available, so mortgaging everything else still leaves an $872 shortfall. Trading for the missing cash would arm another player with a dark blue monopoly, so that path is too risky.

I will end my turn. I will not reveal that I cannot build yet, so I will keep my public message brief and strategic.
